paper.title: Remote Safety Monitoring: Significance-Aware Status Updating for Situational Awareness

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-agent, multi-channel remote safety monitoring RMAB (problem (14)-(15))
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Restless multi-armed bandit planning problem (average-cost MDP with known Markov transition model); no learning/regret; Markovian/restless settings are out of scope.
unmapped: Objective is minimizing long-run average loss (generalized conditional entropy of safety level given latest observation and AoI) in a known-model RMAB
Scheduler pulls at most M of N agents per slot over unreliable channels with success probability p_n
Learner knows transition probabilities, loss functions and channel success probabilities
settings.definition_quote: Our goal is to find a scheduling policy $\pi$ and estimators $\phi_1, \phi_2, \ldots, \phi_N$ that minimize the time-average sum of the expected loss across all $N$ agents ... s.t. \sum_{n=1}^{N} \mu_n (t) \leq M

bound.regime: as the scaling r -> infinity (rN bandits, rM channels)

symbols.r: scaling factor of number of bandits per class and channels

conditions: Assumption 1 (Markov chain structure of safety level and status)
tuning: dual cost lambda* obtained by stochastic subgradient ascent

source.label: optimality
source.quote: Under the uniform global attractor condition in Definition \ref{def2}, the policy \emph{$\pi_{\text{gain}}$} is asymptotically optimal.

results.notes: Asymptotic optimality: gap between MGF average cost and optimal average cost vanishes as system is scaled; expression 0 encodes the gap L_gain - L_opt. Not a regret bound; known-model planning.
